SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

unclear adjective

not known for certain

also uncertain, it’s unclear whether, it isn’t clear, unknown

classical

Cic. Sen. 74: et incertum an hoc ipsō diē
Plin. Ep. 4.11.5 (Lewis & Short): incertum, utrum quia vērum erat

incertus, incerta, incertum

adjective; incertum est with a question: it is unclear whether …

uncertain, not known for sure

Other words

  • dubius, dubia, dubium — doubtful, uncertain; dubium est, it is uncertain

    adjective; dubium est with a question · also used · classical · Varr. LL 6.5: multīs dubium

    See doubt.

  • nōn liquet — it is not clear, not proven

    impersonal of liqueō, alone or with a question · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.6: dē quō Panaetiō nōn liquet

    First the verdict of a juror who could not decide: nōn liquēre dīxērunt (Cic. Clu. 76, Lewis & Short). Liquet, it is clear (Plaut., Cic.).

Examples

  • moriendum enim certē est, et incertum an hoc ipsō diē

    for die we certainly must, and it is uncertain whether it may not be this very dayCic. Sen. 74

  • quod crepusculum diēs etiam nunc sit an jam nox multīs dubium

    because at dusk many are unsure whether it is still day or already nightVarr. LL 6.5

  • praesertim cum id, dē quō Panaetiō nōn liquet, reliquīs ejusdem disciplīnae sōlis lūce videātur clārius

    especially since what is unclear to Panaetius seems clearer than daylight to the rest of his schoolCic. Div. 1.6

See also doubt, sure, unclear, know.
